that the interest of justice would be subserved if we direct the
Trial Court to take up and dispose of the application filed under
Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 of the CPC within a period of two months from
today.

continue. It is made clear that we have not expressed any opinion

registered at Kherwadi Police Station, Mumbai
for the offences punishable under Sections 75,
78, and 79 of The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
and 67 of The Information Technology Act, 2000.

granted interim protection to the petitioner
and the petitioner was also directed to appear
before the Investigation Officer. A detailed
reply has been filed in the matter and learned
counsel for the respondent-State of Maharashtra
has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of
anticipatory bail. However, learned counsel
for the respondent-State has stated before this
Court  that  the  petitioner  is  co-
operating/appearing  before  the  Investigating
Officer.
3.  This Court keeping in view the totality
of  circumstances  and  material  available  on
record and the fact that the petitioner is co-

opinion that the interim order dated 02.06.026

condition that the petitioner shall continue to
co-operate with the investigation and shall
report as and when called upon to do so by the

disposed of in the above terms.

Court has virtually passed an order in the nature of a
final relief, while deciding a Miscellaneous Application
in the Writ Petition.

disposal of the main Writ Petition by the High Court. We
also request the High Court to dispose of the main Writ
Petition within a period of three months from today.

influenced by the observations made in the impugned
order.  All the contentions raised are left open to be
adjudicated upon in the main Writ Petition pending before

Date : 06-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K. VINOD CHANDRAN

                   Ms. S. Ramamani, AOR                   
For Respondent(s) : 
Mr. Zulfiker Ali PS, AOR
    Ms. Lebina Baby, Adv.
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned. 
2. Exemption Application is allowed.
3. By  a  Judgment  dated  29.11.2002  passed  by  the  learned
Additional  Sessions  Judge  (Adhoc)  Fast  Track  Court  II,
Pathanamthitta the petitioner was convicted for murdering his
wife under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC)
and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life.
4. The Petitioner is challenging the judgment and order dated
11.03.2005 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court of
Kerala at Ernakulam by which Criminal Appeal No. 577 of 2003

--- Page 433 ---
2
filed  by  the  petitioner  was  dismissed  by  upholding  his
conviction. 
5. Having gone through the orders passed by the trial court and
the High Court, we are convinced that there is no good ground
to interfere with the conviction and sentence passed against
the petitioner.
6. The petitioner has undergone 24 years of incarceration. By our
Order dated 17.07.2026, we had directed the respondent - State
to submit a report of petitioner’s conduct during the said
period of incarceration and the status of the family members
of the wife, i.e., the deceased.
7. Learned Advocate for the respondent - State had filed an
affidavit on behalf of the State wherein it has been stated
that the petitioner has undergone 24 years, 5 months and 20
days of imprisonment as of 31.7.2026 (inclusive of the period
of remand setoff). The petitioner’s case was considered for
remission by the Prison Advisory Board and recommended on five
occasions from 2017, and in 2019 it was not recommended and in
2025, it stood deferred. Again on 18.08.2025 though his
release was recommended by the Board, the petitioner is
languishing in jail and it is stated that the Home (B)
Department of Kerala directed the matter be placed again
before the Committee for consideration after the constitution
of the new Prison Advisory Committee. The meeting of the newly
constituted Committee is scheduled on 13.08.2026. 
8. We are of the opinion that considering the long incarceration
of the petitioner as well as successive recommendations not
being acted upon, the petitioner ought to be released on bail.
We direct that the petitioner be released on the condition
that he would not indulge in any criminal activities. The
petitioner shall appear before the Additional Sessions Judge
(Adhoc)  Fast  Track  Court  II,  Pathanamthitta  (or  the
Jurisdictional Court) on execution of personal bond with the
above condition, he shall stand released. Any violation of the
conditions would enable the State Police to bring it to the

--- Page 434 ---
3
notice of the Sessions Court so as to take the petitioner back
into custody. 
9. If the Prison Advisory Board advises remission on 13.08.2026,
the bail bond shall stand cancelled. However, if the Board
arrives at an adverse view, the State is at liberty to move an
application in the present SLP.
10. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of. 
11. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

DEPUTY REGISTRAR                                 COURT MASTER (NSH)

1. This petition seeks Special Leave to Appeal against the
impugned judgment and order dated 30.03.2026 passed by the
Single Bench of the High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at
Jaipur  in  S.B.  Criminal  Misc  Suspension  of  Sentence
Application No.69/2026 in S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No.
266/2026, whereby the High Court rejected the petitioner’s

--- Page 436 ---
2
application for suspension of sentence during the pendency of
his revision petition. 
2. By Judgment dated 17.12.2025 passed by the learned Juvenile
Justice  Board  No.-01  Jaipur  Metropolitan,  declared  the
petitioner a law violator under Section 376 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and Sections 3/4, 5(i) (ii)/6 of the
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO)
Act and  sentenced him to a special home for 3 (three) years
and a fine of Rs. 1500/-. The aforesaid judgment was affirmed
in appeal by a judgment dated 30.01.2026 passed by the learned
Special Court; Protection of Children from Sexual Offences
Act, 2012 and Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act,
2005, No. 01, Jaipur Metropolitan-II. The Petitioner has
served more than 2 years, 3 months, in judicial custody till
he was granted interim bail by our order dated 11.05.2026.
3. Having heard learned counsel for both parties and having
perused the material on record, without expressing any final
opinion on the merits of the appeal, we are of the considered
view that a prima facie case for suspension of sentence is
made out, given the minority of the petitioner at the time of
the alleged offence, the custody period undergone, absence of
prior  antecedents,  and  the  arguable  legal  issues  raised
regarding the nature of the act in question.
4. Accordingly, the execution of the substantive sentence of
custody in a special home awarded to the petitioner (Child in
Conflict  with  Law  CA)  in  FIR  No.78/2024,  P.S.  Harmada,
District Jaipur, Rajasthan shall remain suspended during the
pendency of the revision before the High Court.
5. The  Petitioner  shall  be  continued  on  bail,  if  already
released. If not, the Juvenile Justice Board shall release the
petitioner on bail on such conditions as deemed fit and
appropriate, on the basis of the suspension of sentence
granted by us. In the event of breach of any conditions
specified above, it shall be open to the State to move an
application before the Board for cancellation of bail.

--- Page 437 ---
3
6. The Special Leave Petition is disposed of in the above terms.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

3. However, learned counsel for the petitioner draws
attention to para 67 (page 61 pdf 83) of the judgment
dated 8th June, 2018 of the 1 st Additional Sessions Judge,
Special Court under POCSO Act, Thalassery which reads as
follows:
“67. The accused was heard on the question
of sentence.  Considering the totality of the
facts and circumstances of the case, the accused
is sentenced to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for
14  (Fourteen)  years  and  to  pay  fine  of
₹1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) u/s.376 of
IPC, in default of payment of fine to undergo a
further period of Rigorous Imprisonment for one
year and to undergo Rigorous Imprisonment for 14
(Fourteen) years and to pay fine of ₹1,00,000/-
(Rupees One Lakh only) u/s. 5(j)(ii), 5(1) and
5(n) r/s Sec.6 of Protection of Children from
Sexual Offences Act, in default of payment of
fine to undergo a further period of Rigorous
Imprisonment  for  one  year.   The  substantive
sentences will run concurrently.  The default
sentences, if undergone, will run consecutively.
The fine amount, if realised, will be paid as
compensation to PW1 u/s.357(1)(b) of Cr.P.C.  The
period of detention already undergone by the
accused from 03.04.2015 till 08.06.2018 will be
set  off  against  the  substantive  term  of
imprisonment.”
2

--- Page 464 ---
4. Learned counsel referring to Section 42 of the
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
(for short 'the POCSO Act') contends that under the
statute, the Court is obliged to impose a punishment
which is greater in degree but cannot impose sentences
for both under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
and Sections 5 and 6 of the POCSO Act.  When it is
pointed out to the learned counsel that sentences are
concurrent, the learned counsel submits that fine of
Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh) has been imposed on two
counts.
5. Issue notice to consider this aspect.
6. Mr.Aljo K.Joseph, learned counsel accepts notice on
behalf of the respondent-State.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The present petition calls in question the correctness of
the order dated  04-02-2026 in Misc.Civil Case No. 4095/2025
passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Gwalior. By the
said order, the prayer of the petitioner to transfer the case

--- Page 556 ---
2
bearing R.C.S.H.M.No.848/2025 titled as  "Ashish Bansal vs.
Poonam Sharma ”,  pending before the Family Court, Gwalior,
Madhya Pradesh to the Family Court, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh,
was rejected.
2. None appears for the respondent in spite of service of
notice.
3. Having  heard  learned  counsel  appearing  for  the
petitioner, we are inclined to transfer the case sought for.
4. Accordingly,  the  present  Special  Leave  Petition  is
disposed  of  by  transferring  the  case  bearing
R.C.S.H.M.No.848/2025  titled  as  "Ashish  Bansal  vs.  Poonam
Sharma”, from the Family Court, Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh to the
Family Court, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.
5. However, if the video conferencing facility is available
with the Court, the benefit of the same shall be extended to
the parties, unless their physical presence is required.
6. The transferor Court shall forthwith transmit the record
of the aforesaid case to the transferee court.
7. The transferee Court shall make all possible endeavours
first for an amicable settlement between the parties, failing
which for early decision in the matter without unnecessary
adjournments.
8. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of. 
(NIRMALA NEGI)                                  (MANOJ KUMAR)

PETITION(S) FOR SPECIAL LEAVE TO APPEAL (C)  NO(S).  8344/2026
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 15-07-2025
in WA No. 475/2021 passed by the High Court of Andhra Pradesh at
Amravati]
PAGOLU NAGARAJU                                    Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE STATE OF ANDHRA PRADESH & ORS.                 Respondent(s)
IA No. 48955/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
 
WITH
SLP(C) No. 16571/2026 (XII-A)
IA No. 130127/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF THE IMPUGNED 
JUDGMENT
 
Date : 06-08-2026 These matters were called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MANOJ MISRA
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIJAY BISHNOI
For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Sumanth Nookala, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) :Mr. Devadatt Kamat, Sr. Adv.
                   Ms. Prerna Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Guntur Pramod Kumar, AOR
                   Mr. Hruday Bajentri, Adv.
                   Ms. Vanshika Singh, Adv.
                                      
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             
O R D E R
1. By the order impugned the High Court, though upheld the
order of the learned Single Judge setting aside termination and
directing reinstatement, set a condition for reinstatement,
1

--- Page 708 ---
that is, the petitioners would have to pass the physical
fitness test.  It is this condition which has been impugned in
the present petition.
2. The petitioners contended that the impugned condition
defeats the very basis of the order as it gives a handle to
defeat the order of reinstatement by giving a right to reject
the person on medical ground when that fitness was tested at
the time of joining service.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that
the petitioners are required to perform functions akin to
police service and, therefore, fitness is a must. Besides, the
High Court of Andhra Pradesh in its order dated 08.06.2018
passed in a similar proceeding had laid an identical condition
for reinstatement which was accepted by this Court in another
proceeding  i.e.,  Special  Leave  Petition  (Civil)  Diary
No.45455/2018 preferred by the Government of Telangana against
a similar order of reinstatement.
4. Having regard to the fact that condition to undergo
fitness test was affirmed by this Court in another proceeding,
we decline to entertain these special leave petitions. The
petitions are, accordingly, dismissed.
5. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
  (KAVITA PAHUJA)                               (SAPNA BANSAL)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Exemption Application is allowed.
2. The petitioner, has been in custody since 10.10.2025 and has
been denied regular bail by the High Court in connection with
FIR  No.  0433/2024  registered  with  Police  Station  Kotma,
District Anuppur for the offences punishable under Sections 8,
20(B)& 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances

--- Page 930 ---
2
Act, 1985(for short “NDPS”).
3. The Petitioner is accused of attempting to transport 64.77 kg
of ganja from Manendragarh towards Anuppur for sale.
4. A charge-sheet has been filed in this case, wherein it has
been recorded that the petitioner was amongst the co-accused
seated in a car carrying aforesaid quantity of the contraband
and fled when that car was apprehended by the police. The
charges have been framed against the petitioner for the
aforesaid  offences,  and  the  trial  is  in  progress.  The
prosecution has proposed to examine 19 witnesses out of which
only 4 have been examined so far. The other three co-accused
in the case have been enlarged on bail.          
5. On a prima facie consideration of the materials on record and
after hearing the learned counsel for the parties, we are of
the opinion that the petitioner can be released on bail,
subject to such terms and conditions that the Special Judge
(‘NDPS ACT’) ANU PPUR, Madhya Pradesh may deem fit to impose.
Ordered accordingly. The petitioner shall cooperate with the
trial.
6. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
